title: Hagen–Poiseuille flow in a round pipe with interpolated walls (Bouzidi et al.)
source: Hagen–Poiseuille flow driven by a body force a in a pipe of radius R: u(r) = a (R² − r²) / (4 ν), u_max = a R² / (4 ν); walls by M. Bouzidi, M. Firdaouss, P. Lallemand, Phys. Fluids 13(11):3452–3459, 2001, doi:10.1063/1.1399290

quantities.quantity: centreline velocity a R² / (4 ν), 8 cells per radius
quantities.reason: interpolated walls at 8 cells per radius: measured −0.15 %, converging at second order (−0.04 % at 16; the README's table); a third of the tolerance. Halfway walls read −5.5 % here, so the case fails if the obstacle's links fall back to halfway bounce-back
quantities.fixture_reason: the pipe wall comes from a SolidCraft design: its triangulation is not bit-identical across platforms, though q is taken on the exact cylinder

quantities.quantity: centreline velocity a R² / (4 ν), 16 cells per radius
quantities.reason: interpolated walls at 16 cells per radius: measured −0.04 %, a quarter of the tolerance; halfway walls read −2.1 %
quantities.fixture_reason: the pipe wall comes from a SolidCraft design: its triangulation is not bit-identical across platforms, though q is taken on the exact cylinder
